standard_prerequisites.name: Tableau derivability
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma derives A when some finite signed set with the negation of A at prefix 1 and the B_i of Gamma at prefix 1 has a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the finite signed set Delta the proof works with (2157-2161).

standard_prerequisites.name: Tableau soundness
standard_prerequisites.statement: A signed set with a closed tableau is unsatisfiable; the unit proves this as its soundness theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: It contradicts the satisfying interpretation built in the proof (2165-2168).

standard_prerequisites.name: Interpretation of prefixes
standard_prerequisites.statement: An interpretation of the prefixes of a branch into a model maps each prefix to a world; the root prefix may be sent to any world.
standard_prerequisites.use: Mapping prefix 1 to the countermodel world w makes the model satisfy Delta with respect to it (2163-2165).

core_obligations: From Gamma derives A, form the finite signed set Delta with the negated A and the finite support B_1, ..., B_n of Gamma, having a closed tableau (2157-2161).
Suppose Gamma does not entail A: take a model M and world w with all B_i true at w and A false at w (2161-2163).
Build the interpretation of the prefixes of Delta into M by mapping prefix 1 to w, so M satisfies Delta with respect to it (2163-2165).
The tableau soundness theorem declares Delta unsatisfiable, a contradiction; hence Gamma entails A (2165-2170).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack derivability into a closed tableau for a finite signed set.
Assume a countermodel and interpret the root prefix into it.
Contradict the soundness theorem and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted corollary is the author corollary at source lines 2153-2155: if Gamma derives A in the prefixed tableau calculus then Gamma entails A. The author proof (2157-2170) unpacks the signed-set definition of derivability into a closed tableau for a finite signed set, runs the contrapositive by assuming a countermodel at a world, builds an interpretation of the branch's prefixes into that model by mapping the root prefix to the world, invokes the unit's tableau soundness theorem to declare the closed tableau unsatisfiable, and closes by contradiction. Constructing the prefix interpretation and keeping the signed formulas aligned is the counted work.
